If I had to rate this one I'd give it a 6/10 - it's starting to show it's age and is of the mid 2010's era where every Ubisoft game had it's tranch of collectibles, radiotowers and outposts to take over. Don't get me wrong, the setting is unique and actually was pretty daring to try, and, for the most part, I think it paid off. There are few prehistoric games out there and if you want to get immersed in such a context, this game does a pretty good job. 

That being said, I found the story to be pretty weak - it basically amounts to build up this Wenja village and defeat the heads of two tribes. Along the way, recruit some other folk and gather all the resources that you can find in order to unlock upgrades for your weapons. The animal taming mechanic is quite unique and riding around on a mammoth is fun for the first few times however the game quickly falls into a very formulaic experience. Generally, gameplay will involve trying to stealth an outpost or bonfire however you'll quickly fail owing to enemies having x-ray vision. You'll then charge in swinging your two handed axe whilst also having no ability to dodge spears or arrows and therefore be hamming the health button constantly. The bow is also your friend along with berserk/sting bombs but outside of this, the other weapons and gadgetry that a pre-historic setting can offer is fairly pointless. 

The world feels alive, mainly due to the mad respawn rate on animals so it feels like a day out at a petting zoo however you will be attacked every 5 seconds by something. The environments are ok, but again due to the setting, outside of some caves and wooden shelters and the odd standing stone, there's not much of actual interest in the world. I almost feel like having Far Cry attached to the game holds it back somewhat as you can't help but compare it against some of the more interesting locales that the modern iterations provide.

In 2026, Far Cry Primal is still worth a play on sale but don't waste your time chasing all the collectibles and pointless recurrent Wenja activities. Stick to the main story, handful of side quests, upgrading the village, weapons and animal taming and then call it a day.

Одобряю. Отличный эксперимент и достойный экспонат в коллекцию.
Самый странный Far Cry в серии. Изначально я смотрел его только в летсплеях на YouTube и не очень понимал сути. Фундамент-то у игры абсолютно стандартный: всё та же знакомая карта области и типичные сюжетные моменты. Но вместо привычного огнестрела нам выдали палки, копья да луки с разными стрелами. Также здесь появилась переработанная механика напарников-животных - судя по всему, это была своего рода проба пера перед полноценным внедрением этой фичи в Far Cry 5.
Не сказать, что эта часть получилась очень длинной, и не сказать, что сюжет здесь прям захватывающий. Но в качестве экспоната для коллекции любимой серии проект вышел вполне играбельным. Скоротать время в первобытном сеттинге можно с большим удовольствием.
Итоговые оценки:
Сеттинг и концепт: 8 из 10. Каменный век, мамонты, саблезубые тигры и воюющие племена - смелый шаг для Ubisoft. Мир выглядит диким, красивым и по-своему опасным. 
Боевая система: 7 из 10. Стрельба из лука сделана приятно, а вот ближний бой с дубинками получился немного топорным. Тем не менее швырять копья в доисторических врагов надоедает не сразу. 
Механика приручения: 8 из 10. Возможность приручить дикого зверя и натравить его на вражеский аванпост - лучшее, что есть в игре. Кататься верхом на саблезубом тигре или медведе действительно весело.
P.S. Самое хардкорное и пугающее в этой игре - вовсе не огромные мамонты или саблезубые тигры. Настоящий ужас первобытного мира - это маленькие, яростные проклятые куницы переростки называемые медоедами. Эти проклятые барсуки плевать хотели на твои копья и стрелы, они просто идут уничтожать всё живое на своем пути.

Far Cry Primal me ha parecido un juego bastante divertido y más que recomendable por el precio al que suele estar hoy en día. En mi caso me costó solo 2,99€ y sinceramente por ese precio es difícil arrepentirse.

La ambientación prehistórica es lo mejor del juego. El mapa es muy variado, con zonas nevadas, bosques y áreas más áridas, y además el clima afecta a la jugabilidad, ya que en algunas zonas necesitas ropa especial y para conseguirla tienes que cazar animales como mamuts. También me gustó mucho la fauna: tigres dientes de sable, mamuts y otros animales hacen que el juego se sienta diferente al resto de Far Cry.

La historia no me llegó a enganchar del todo, pero sí me pareció interesante por cómo presenta las distintas tribus y la evolución humana. La jugabilidad es muy sencilla y fácil de aprender; de hecho me adapté rapidísimo viniendo de Far Cry 3 y apenas morí durante la partida. Eso sí, se nota que es un juego de 2016: muchas mecánicas son simples y repetitivas, con bastantes misiones secundarias de recolectar o cazar.

Gráficamente sigue viéndose bastante bien, especialmente la iluminación y las noches, que consiguen crear una atmósfera muy inmersiva. De noche el juego cambia completamente y aparecen más animales peligrosos, algo que me pareció muy divertido.

No diría que sea un juego muy rejugable porque desplazarse puede hacerse algo lento al no haber vehículos, pero como experiencia única merece bastante la pena. La historia principal me duró unas 22 horas y terminé satisfecho.

En general, un buen juego sin más pretensiones: entretenido, diferente y con una ambientación muy original. Mi nota sería un 7/10.

FCP is an open-world, survival game that tackles community crises and you, as the chosen one, enacts genocide on neighbouring communities that don't align with you. I did a platinum run getting all achievements including the SOTF ones. The game overall is easy and chill unless it's SOTF, then it's really hard but realistic. 

Pros: 
- voice acting and language of the people is fine. The SFX is also good. Music is good. Nothing crazy on either ends of the spectrum. 
- combat system is seamless and good. You'll realize quickly which items are the OP ones, especially takedowns and poison. Skill system is also good tho some skills are frankly pointless imo but others are imperative to success and having fun. Even getting the achievements for the combat is not that grindy. But, can be slow-paced due to the meticulousness and planning needed.. but if you like that tho..
- the world design is good. The game is expansive, having you explore the northern savages and the southern arsonists. As you'd expect, much of the game is running around and to make it more exciting, there are collectibles along the way. Caves are annoying tho. 
- the collectibles are cool but some are a bit much. Doesn't need to be that much for a 100% but for the platinum, you only need to collect just under half of all collectibles; very doable and not that tedious. Collecting the rest just gives XP for levelling up though there is a level cap. 
- animal life is cool. Taming animals and finding the rare animals is cool, kinda like pokemon. The AI of the tamed beasts are also good and not as clunky (though it makes a big difference in SOTF). 

Cons: 
- quite repetitive in terms of map design. A lot of everything, looks like everything else. It is realistic but unfortunately, reality can be boring. This is especially true for the caves. 
- this one character, Urki? Bro he sounds so fcking lame. Where other characters sound good and is more immersive, this dude just sounds like some American tourist mocking the language of the locals. He deserves a con. 


Overall, it's a good game. It's not a bad game to get most achievements. SOTF is for hardcore players that you really need to prepare for and plan. Otherwise, all other achievements isn't so hard or bad. And for its base price, I think it's reasonable. A run that accomplishes all other achievements would be like 30 hours. Double that or more for SOTF bc that sht is tough, but it's supposed to be.
